name: Registered Item Model
abstract:
A base RDF and SHACL model for register items, register item classes and register
governance metadata, aligned with ISO 19135:2026 (*Geographic information — Registration
and register governance*). Sub-registers profile this model rather than inventing their own.
description:
A register is a catalogue with systematic governance: a content information model
(what an item looks like) plus management metadata (who governs it, what state it is
in, how it changes). ISO 19135:2026 defines one such register model — separating a
**concept plane** (meaning: concepts and concept versions) from a **content plane**
(representation: register item classes and register items) and adding a governance
layer of roles, statuses, actions and commitments.

This repository publishes that model as a single base [OGC Building
Block](https://ogcincubator.github.io/bblocks-docs/), independent of any one register's
own content schema. Any register — a CSV catalogue, the OGC Definitions Server, a
GitHub-managed vocabulary, or a Building Blocks register itself — maps its own
schema's identifiers, statuses and roles onto this base model via a JSON-LD context,
so that management metadata from otherwise unrelated registers becomes one queryable
graph. A sub-register's rules are expressed as a profile of this base block (null,
additive, or constrained), always validating against it.

Register vs. registry: the **register** is the governed information (items,
identifiers, statuses, roles, processes); the **register system** — often loosely
called the "registry" — is merely the information system it happens to run on. This
model describes the former, independent of the latter.

bblocks.name: Registered Item Model
bblocks.title: Base RDF/OWL and SHACL model for register items and register governance
bblocks.abstract: A base RDF and SHACL model for register items, register item classes and register governance metadata, based on ISO 19135:2026.
bblocks.description: A register is a catalogue distinguished from a plain dataset by systematic governance: a content information model (register item classes and register items) plus management metadata (identifiers, statuses, actions, roles). ISO 19135:2026 defines one such model, separating a concept plane (meaning) from a content plane (representation) and adding roles, statuses, actions, relations and commitments on top. This block publishes that model as a single base building block so that many registers with different native schemas — a CSV catalogue, the OGC Definitions Server, a GitHub-managed vocabulary, or a Building Blocks register itself — can each map their own fields onto it via a JSON-LD context, and be queried as one graph. Sub-registers are expected to profile this block (null, additive or constrained) rather than invent their own register model.

bblocks.name: ML Activity Profile
bblocks.title: Machine learning training/inference activities, profiled from the Registered Item Model
bblocks.abstract: A profile of the Registered Item Model describing machine learning training and inference runs as typed register actions, using the STAC MLM extension's task, framework/accelerator and input/output vocabulary.
bblocks.description: The STAC Machine Learning Model (MLM) extension describes a model as a static artifact — a STAC Item or Collection with declared inputs, outputs and requirements — but has no notion of a particular run of that model. This block adds that: mlact:MLActivity (with mlact:TrainingActivity and mlact:InferenceActivity sub-types) is a rim:RegisterAction, and so a prov:Activity, recording one execution. In this ecosystem, running a model is itself a governed act — typically the one that adds a derived product to a register as a new rim:RegisterItem — so the run belongs in the same audit trail as any other register action. The activity's task, framework and accelerator are drawn from the MLM extension's own SKOS schemes rather than redefined, and its recorded inputs/outputs (mlact:ActivityInput / mlact:ActivityOutput, both prov:Entity) each declare via dct:conformsTo which of the model's own declared mlm:ModelInput/mlm:ModelOutput specifications they realise.
